Alternate Base64 spellings do not bypass CivicCast authorization: subscription HMAC verifies the decoded bytes, AES-GCM authenticates the decoded envelope, and paywall signatures verify canonical parsed payload bytes. They do not authorize by the textual Base64 spelling or forward it to a different decoder. Installer/signature inputs use validate=True. The upstream change is an alphabet-deprecation warning, not a cryptographic fix.

No cross-decoder authorization boundary: subscription/AES-GCM/paywall authenticate the decoded payload itself. Untrusted signed-package, federation and recovery inputs use validate=True. Other permissive calls consume locally generated worker commands, stored salts, or already-validated timestamp proofs, not a second interpretation of attacker-controlled trailing data.

The vulnerability requires XML_ParserReset reuse of one native parser. Pinned CPython pyexpat.c and _elementtree.c neither call nor expose XML_ParserReset; each parser is created with XML_ParserCreate_MM. Stdlib SAX reset constructs another ParserCreate object. Actual shipped3.12.16/Expat2.9.0 exposes no Reset method. This is API non-reachability, not a claim that Expat2.9.0 fixes the issue.

Supported untrusted CAP/RSS XML parsing uses existing defusedxml with forbid_dtd=True and forbid_entities=True, aborting at the DTD declaration before entity amplification. The overread is only in the unknown-encoding path for multi-byte lead bytes (map value -2..-4) that calls the application convert callback. Pinned CPython 3.12.16 PyUnknownEncodingHandler decodes exactly 256 single bytes, rejects multi-byte encodings with ValueError, sets every map entry to a code point or -1, and sets convert=NULL, so no multi-byte lead entry exists and the vulnerable branch is unreachable. libexpat 2.11.0 was released on 2026-11-23 and fixes this CVE, but the shipped CPython 3.12.16 still vendors Expat 2.10.0 and was not upgraded in rc.8. This is API non-reachability, not a claim that Expat 2.10.0 fixes the issue.

The overread needs an application-registered unknown encoding handler. The shipped libexpat.dll is consumed only by fontconfig-1.dll, whose resolved PE imports do not include XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler, and Fontconfig 2.16.1 fcxml.c creates a UTF-8 XML_ParserCreate parser without one. The vulnerable decoder path is unreachable. libexpat 2.11.0 was released on 2026-11-23 and fixes this CVE, but the shipped libexpat.dll remains 2.10.0 and was not upgraded in rc.8; no underlying version fix is claimed.

http.cookies.Morsel accepts a separator semicolon inside attribute values, which could relax the Domain or SameSite restriction. CivicCast sets exactly two cookies, both through starlette.responses.Response.set_cookie (starlette 1.3.1, which builds http.cookies.SimpleCookie). No caller passes an attacker-controlled attribute value: paywall/router.py:780 uses the literal key civiccast_viewer, no domain, literal path /api/public, literal samesite=strict and a value of base64url(JSON)+'.'+hex HMAC (paywall/service.py:_encode_token, alphabet A-Za-z0-9-_ and '.', no semicolon). schedule/router.py:679 uses a cookie name of sha256(asset_id)[:16] hex, a value of secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (A-Za-z0-9-_), literal samesite=strict, and path /media/staff-source/{asset_id}/ where asset_id passed the ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,63}$ fullmatch before the grant was issued. No other set_cookie, delete_cookie or raw Set-Cookie writer exists in civiccast/. The upstream fix is only in 3.16.0.
